senses.gloss:
तृष् 1. तृष्, cl. 4. P. तृष्यति, ततर्ष
(Ved. 3rd pl. तातृषुस्, part. तातृषाण),
अतर्षत्, तर्षितुम्, to be thirsty, to thirst; to
thirst for (metaphorically), desire, long for: Caus.
तर्षयति, -यितुम्, to cause to thirst; [cf. Zend
tarṣṇa, ‘thirst;’ Goth. thars, ‘to become dry;’
thairsa, thars, thaursum; thaursus, ‘dry;’ thaurs-
tei, ‘thirst;’ thaursyan, ‘to thirst;’ ga-thaurs-
an-s, ‘dry:’ Angl. Sax. thurst, thyrr: Old Germ.
darran, ‘to become dry:’ Germ. durst: Gr. τέρσ-
ο-μαι, τερσαίνω, ταρσός, ταρσ-ιά, τρασ-ιά: Lat.
torreo for torseo, tos-tum from tors-tum, torris,
torrens: Lith. tróksztu, ‘to thirst;’ trószkulis,
‘thirst:’ Hib. tart (tar-t), ‘thirst, drought;’ tart-
mhar, ‘thirsty, dry.’]

2. तृष्, ट्, f. thirst; thirst after (metaphorically),
wish, strong desire; Desire personified as a daughter
of the god of Love (Kāma).

तृषा, f. thirst; strong desire or wish; Desire
personified as a daughter of Kāma; a poisonous
plant, Methonica Superba (लाङ्गलिकी).
—तृषा-
भू, ऊस्, f. the bladder (whence thirst exists or
arises).
—तृषा-रोग, अस्, m. ‘morbid thirst,’ N. of
a particular disease.
—तृषार्त (˚षा-आर्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, suffering from thirst, thirsty; affected by desire.
—तृषा-ह, अम्, n. water (destroying or quenching
thirst); (आ), f. a kind of anise, = मधुरिका.
तृषाण, अस्, आ, अम्, (Ved. part.) being thirsty.

तृषित, अस्, आ, अम्, thirsty, thirsting (physically
or metaphorically); (अम्), n. thirst, desire.
—तृ-
षितोत्तरा (˚त-उत्˚), f., N. of a plant, = अशन-
पर्णी.
तृषित्वा or तर्षित्वा, ind. having become thirsty.

तृषु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. greedy, libidinous, thirst-
ing for, eagerly desirous; rushing violently, quick.
—तृषु-च्यवस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. moving rapidly
or quickly.
—तृषु-च्युत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. quickly
issuing, rapidly moving.
तृष्णक, अस्, आ, अम्, said to = तृष्णज्.

तृष्णज्, क्, क्, क्, thirsty (physically or meta-
phorically), desiring, longing for, cupidinous; [cf.
अ-तृष्णज्.]

तृष्णा, f. (in the Veda the accent is on the first
syllable, in later Sanskrit on the last), thirst, strong
wish, desire, avidity; (Tṛṣṇā and Lobha are some-
times personified as the parents of Dambha; or
Tṛṣṇā is variously regarded as a daughter of Death,
or of Pāpīyas, or as generated by Vedanā and gene-
rating Upādāna); [cf. अति-तृष्ण.]
—तृष्णा-
क्षय, अस्, m. cessation of desire, tranquillity of
mind, resignation, patience, content.
—तृष्णा-घ्न,
अस्, ई, अम्, quenching the thirst.
—तृष्णामय
(˚णा-आम्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, ill with thirst.
—तृष्णा-
मार, अस्, m., Ved. dying of thirst.
—तृष्णारि
(˚णा-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of thirst,’ a kind of plant
(= पर्पट).
तृष्णालु, उस्, उस्, उ, thirsting much, very thirsty.
तृष्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, thirsting, athirst; desiring.

तृष्या, f., Ved. thirst.
—तृष्या-वत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, Ved. thirsty; [cf. तर्ष्या-वत्.]

तृष्ट तृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. rough, harsh;
pungent; rugged; hoarse.
—तृष्ट-जम्भ, अस्,
आ, अम्, Ved. having rough or uneven teeth.
—तृष्ट-
दंश्मन्, आ, आ, अ, Ved. biting roughly.
—तृष्ट-
धूम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having pungent breath,
epithet of a snake.
—तृष्ट-वन्दन, अस्, आ, अम्,
Ved. one whose praise is distasteful.
—तृष्टामा
(˚ट-अम्˚), f., Ved. N. of a river.

तृष्ट, to be connected with rt. 1. तृष्; add
 — (originally) dry.

तृष्टिका, f., Ved. rough, disagreeable, epithet of
a woman.
